original_question: For the two real 1-parameter families of irreducible G2-instantons described in Theorem 3 on the SU(3)-bundle Q over Lambda^2_-(CP^2), what is the limiting behavior of these G2-instantons as the parameter c tends to +infinity?
target_in_paper: Open problem (d) in §3.3: "What is the limit as c → +∞ of the G2-instantons in Theorem 3?" ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct object, setting, and parameter regime: it points to the two 1-parameter families from Theorem 3, places them on the Bryant–Salamon CP^2 example, names the SU(3)-bundle Q, and asks exactly about the regime c → +∞. That is essentially the same question the paper isolates as an open problem in §3.3(d). ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
missing_details: The paper presents this as an open problem in §3.3(d), not as a proved theorem or conjecture, so a paper-faithful stand-alone version should say so explicitly. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the bundle should be defined explicitly as Q = SU(3) ×_{U(1)^2} SU(3), with U(1)^2 acting diagonally on both SU(3) factors through a fixed maximal torus. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The ambient manifold should be named explicitly as X = Lambda^2_-(CP^2) with its Bryant–Salamon asymptotically conical G2-holonomy metric; the radial variable s used in Theorem 3 is the Euclidean distance along the fibers to the zero section. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The notation entering Theorem 3 is implicit in your draft: the decomposition su(3) = u(1)^2 ⊕ C_{α1} ⊕ C_{α2} ⊕ C_{α3}, the fixed invariant maps/forms l and λ_i, and the function u_c(s) should be referenced if the question is to stand on its own. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The main unresolved ambiguity is the meaning of 'limit': the paper itself does not specify the topology or whether gauge transformations are allowed, so a sharp stand-alone formulation should at least say 'up to gauge' and indicate a natural gauge-theoretic mode of convergence. The paper uses smooth convergence on compact subsets when it analyzes similar parameter limits elsewhere. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The algebraic metadata from your general rubric (ambient ring/field, degree, nilpotency, 'for all sufficiently large m', etc.) are not applicable here; the omitted data are geometric rather than algebraic. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
refined_question: Let X = Lambda^2_-(CP^2) be the Bryant–Salamon asymptotically conical G2-manifold, and let Q = SU(3) ×_{U(1)^2} SU(3), where U(1)^2 acts diagonally through a fixed maximal torus. In the notation of §3.1.2, Theorem 3 gives two explicit 1-parameter families of irreducible SU(3)-invariant G2-instantons A_c on Q, written using the decomposition su(3) = u(1)^2 ⊕ C_{α1} ⊕ C_{α2} ⊕ C_{α3}, the invariant forms l and λ_i, the fiber-radius s, and the function u_c(s) = 1 - 2cs^2/(s^2(1 + c) + 2(√(1 + s^2) + 1)), with c ≥ 0. What is the c → +∞ limit of these Theorem 3 instantons, up to gauge transformation, in the natural gauge-theoretic sense? ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
justification: The nearest official target is exactly §3.3(d), which asks for the c → +∞ limit of the instantons from Theorem 3. Theorem 3 in §3.1.2 supplies the precise families and notation, while the surrounding AC discussion explains why limits of G2-instantons are a natural issue on Bryant–Salamon manifolds. Your draft is therefore very close to the paper's actual intent; the only substantial omissions are the explicit definition of Q, the Bryant–Salamon geometric setting and notation, and the otherwise implicit choice of gauge-theoretic notion of convergence. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
